title: Mobile Architecture Migration: Flutter/Dart to React Native + Expo SDK 57
scope: Complete replacement of the Flutter/Dart mobile stack with two independent React Native + Expo SDK 57 + TypeScript apps (Collector, Consumer), including full Flutter/Dart purge, real backend/device_ai API integration, offline-first sync, backend-mediated blockchain/trust verification, accessibility, security review, real tests, and full-system regression.

flutter_dart_purge.removal_commit_message: chore(mobile): remove flutter and dart architecture

git_history_secret_audit.reason: no secrets found; history rewrite not warranted and not authorized

flutter_dart_purge.remaining_flutter_dart_doc_references: intentional 'migrated from Flutter/Dart' historical notes only, in README.md, PROJECT.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/engineering/{01_CLAUDE,03_ARCHITECTURE,12_ROADMAP}.md, plus a disclosed partial-coverage superseded-banner in docs/engineering/07_FRONTEND.md

react_native_implementation.generator: create-expo-app (official Expo tooling, not hand-picked versions)
react_native_implementation.architecture: src/{api,auth,components,config,hooks,navigation,screens,storage,types} per app, TypeScript throughout, no shared codebase between apps
collector_app_features: auth (login, secure-store session persistence, role gate, logout)
AI device classification via POST /devices/register, confirm/finalize
lifecycle actions: accept/start/complete matching real backend state machine
offline-first AsyncStorage queue for AI device confirmations
consumer_app_features: auth (register matching real registerSchema, login, secure-store, role gate, logout)
submission history with offline queue status/retry

real_defects_found_and_fixed.description: Collector app's RegisterDeviceScreen and offline sync queue incorrectly called submissionsApi.create() (POST /submissions), which requires the CONSUMER role per backend/src/modules/submission/submission.routes.ts's real authorize() middleware — a Collector would receive 403
real_defects_found_and_fixed.root_cause: assumption made before reading the real authorization middleware
real_defects_found_and_fixed.fix: removed create()/CreateSubmissionInput from the Collector app's API layer entirely; RegisterDeviceScreen now only confirms/finalizes the AI-side device record (the real authorized Collector action); offline queue re-scoped from 'pending submissions' to 'pending device confirmations'
real_defects_found_and_fixed.verification_method: direct inspection of submission.routes.ts's authorize(UserRole.X) calls for every endpoint used by either app

blockchain_architecture: Mobile apps never touch Fabric directly. Consumer app's DevicePassportScreen reads exclusively through intelligence/device_ai's REST API (/passport, /trust, /passport/verify), which owns the real FabricGatewayClient validated against a genuine local Fabric network in P9.2. No Fabric SDK, peer address, wallet, or private key exists in either app.

real_ecosystem_findings.finding: @testing-library/react-native 14.0.1's render() returns a Promise on this React 19.2.3 / react-native 0.86.3 / test-renderer stack
real_ecosystem_findings.verification: direct debug instrumentation showed render() returning {} (unresolved Promise) until awaited

real_ecosystem_findings.finding: fireEvent.press/.changeText/.scroll also return Promises on this stack and must be awaited
real_ecosystem_findings.verification: confirmed via fire-event.d.ts's real Promise<void>/Promise<undefined> signatures and an 'overlapping act() calls' warning before the fix

real_ecosystem_findings.finding: eslint-config-expo's flat config enables react-hooks/set-state-in-effect, flagging 4 instances of calling a useCallback-wrapped async function directly from useEffect across both apps
real_ecosystem_findings.fix: inlined the initial fetch in the effect body with a cancelled guard; kept the useCallback version only for explicit manual refresh

accessibility.detail: Every interactive control has accessibilityRole/accessibilityLabel; form inputs use nativeID/accessibilityLabelledBy; busy/disabled states use accessibilityState not color alone; error/status banners use accessibilityRole=alert or accessibilityLiveRegion=polite; 44x44pt minimum touch targets throughout. No live screen-reader (TalkBack/VoiceOver) device walkthrough was performed — no device/emulator exists in this environment.

security_review: Token storage via expo-secure-store (Keychain/Keystore-backed), never AsyncStorage
No hardcoded secrets — API URLs and service API key are EXPO_PUBLIC_* build-time env vars
No Fabric credentials in mobile code
assertSecureApiUrl() throws in release builds if API URLs are not HTTPS (P8.7 pattern)
Logout clears secure storage and calls real POST /auth/logout
No sensitive data logged in production code paths
Client-side validation is UX-only; backend Zod schemas remain the real authority

tests.name: iOS build
tests.detail: requires macOS + Xcode; this is a Windows environment

tests.name: Frontend regression
tests.detail: typecheck clean, lint clean; untouched this phase

e2e_status: PASS WITH LIMITATIONS — screens and API wiring implemented and individually verified against real endpoints/authorization; a live device/emulator tap-through of the full journey was not performed (no Android/iOS runtime in this environment)
performance: BLOCKED — ENVIRONMENT — no physical device or emulator exists to measure startup/navigation/scan-response latency; not fabricated
ci: No pre-existing mobile CI job existed to remove. A new React Native CI job was not added in this phase — disclosed, deliberately deferred to keep scope bounded, not silently omitted.

files_changed.removed: 90 tracked Flutter/Dart files (8337 lines) across both apps, commit 31d40c4

environmental_limitations.detail: Verified via accessibility-prop inspection, not a live device session
Not exercised as a live tap-through

unresolved_issues: None that block a pilot release on the currently-supported platforms (Metro/Expo Go dev, web preview). The Android/iOS build gap is environmental, not a functionality gap.
